rule: Score without assuming sufficiency. Public-investment / prosperity-fund returns are SEPARATE and NOT counted as replacement dollars.

families.title: Resource revenue

members.label: Severance (DFA GR line)
members.notes: Orders of magnitude too small for IIT replacement. Commodity-cycle volatility. Incidence on extractive operators may pass through prices.

members.label: Energy production/export premium (beyond current severance)
members.notes: Not counted as replacement dollars until a legal instrument and magnitude are modeled.

members.label: Land/resource rents
members.notes: Philosophically aligned; no Arkansas magnitude bind this slice.

families.family_verdict: Current bound resource GR (~$10.6M) cannot carry a meaningful share of the $3.859B IIT burden. Resource family remains a study track, not a fill.

families.title: Enterprise / business revenue

members.label: Corporate income tax (gross)
members.notes: Largest bound enterprise stream, still only ~14% of IIT gross even before behavioral response. Rate increases may reduce base (T5). Not sufficient alone.

members.label: Gaming (GR line)
members.notes: Small vs IIT. Incidence often falls on players; earmarks (e.g. Highway Casino Transfer) already claim portions.

members.label: State enterprise / public investment dividends
members.notes: KEEP SEPARATE — do not count toward gap closure this slice.

families.family_verdict: Bound enterprise streams (corporate ~$0.52B + gaming ~$0.06B + franchise ~$0.01B ≈ $0.60B) cover at most ~15% of IIT gross if hypothetically redirected — and they are already funding current GR. Raising them is not free money.

families.title: Consumption revenue

members.label: State sales & use tax (existing stream)
members.notes: Scale is comparable to IIT — but this stream ALREADY funds the state. Using it as IIT replacement requires large rate hikes or spending cuts elsewhere. Default sales-tax swap is a household burden shift.

members.label: Broad consumption tax increase as IIT replacement
members.illustrative: Replacing $3.859B via higher sales tax would require roughly doubling the state's sales/use yield (before elasticity) unless base is broadened aggressively.
members.notes: SURFACED EXPLICITLY: this path shifts burden onto ordinary households through higher prices unless strong household protections (rebates, exempt necessities, progressive credits) are locked first. Not prosperity-aligned by default.

members.label: Tourism / visitor taxes
members.notes: GR tourist line is tiny; local option tourism may be larger but not bound as statewide IIT replacement.

members.label: Consumption with household protections (design gate)
members.notes: Only admissible as a study candidate if incidence analysis shows protections neutralize regressivity. Without that, treat as burden rename.

families.family_verdict: Consumption is the only family with scale near IIT — and that is exactly why a naive sales-tax swap fails the prosperity test. Surface regressivity; do not recommend abolition via silent rate shift.

excluded_from_replacement_dollars.reason: Local ledger hypothesis — not state GR bind

gap_after_bound_non_consumption_redirect.note: Even summing corporate+gaming+franchise+severance (~$0.60B) leaves ~$3.26B of IIT gross uncovered — and those dollars are already spent in the GR system, so 'redirect' is not incremental capacity.
